items.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: And, a singer we had, Helen Humes after that.

ctx.x: Did you have any band boys to help out?

Yeah, we had a band boy named Wilson. He left Kansas City, later on to see Charlie Barnett’s band, stayed with him ‘til he died. And Wilson…he was the valet. He did all the packing of the instruments, drums, bass, everything by himself. And, a singer we had, Helen Humes after that.
How was it having women vocalists on the bus?

items.title: 67255_Helen Humes oral history interview
items.q: They had Benny Goodman, Teddy Wilson, and Milt Harry Hinton, Shelly Mann, / Edison. Lockjaw was there.

ctx.x: Were you with a group? Did you take a group?
No I didn't take a group but a group went. They had Benny Goodman, Teddy Wilson, and Milt Harry Hinton, Shelly Mann, / Edison. Lockjaw was there.
Oh. Was Gus Johnson on that one?

items.title: 67255_Helen Humes oral history interview
items.q: I don't know, of course, Sweets, he was something else.

ctx.x: That must have been pretty hard. And then, I mean, there were all the different personalities in the Band.
Yeah, but they were all so nice. Just the nicest bunch. I don't know, of course, Sweets, he was something else.
